passages.title: 舅舅的大夜班
passages.text: My uncle works as a {1} at a convenience store near our school. He works the night shift, from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. Most people think the store is quiet at night, but it is not. One night, a {2} came in at 3 a.m. in his pajamas. He wanted to buy a birthday cake for his wife. "Her birthday starts in one hour!" he said. My uncle helped him {3} a small cake and some candles. Another time, a high school student came in with only twenty dollars. She could not {4} a hot meal, so she bought a rice ball. My uncle quietly gave her a free cup of soup. "Being kind is part of my job," he told me. I am really {5} of him.

blanks.why: clerk「店員」：舅舅在便利商店當店員。knee（膝蓋）、spoon（湯匙）、fever（發燒）都不是職業，不能用 work as a… 。
customer「顧客」：凌晨三點有位顧客穿著睡衣走進來。noodle（麵）、pumpkin（南瓜）、cough（咳嗽）都不會走進店裡買蛋糕。
help + 人 + 原形動詞：幫他找到 find 一個小蛋糕。spell（拼字）、cough（咳嗽）、shout（大叫）接 a small cake 都不通。
can't afford + 物「買不起某物」：她只有二十元，買不起熱騰騰的一餐。spell、sneeze（打噴嚏）、shout 接 a hot meal 意思都不通。
be proud of + 人「以某人為榮」。thirsty（口渴的）、salty（鹹的）、sour（酸的）都不能接 of him 表示驕傲。

passages.zh: 我舅舅在我們學校附近的便利商店當店員。他上大夜班，從晚上十一點到早上七點。大部分的人以為晚上店裡很安靜，其實不然。有一天晚上，一位顧客凌晨三點穿著睡衣走進來，他想幫太太買生日蛋糕。「她的生日再一個小時就到了！」他說。舅舅幫他找到一個小蛋糕和幾根蠟燭。還有一次，一個高中生只帶了二十元進來，她買不起一份熱食，只好買一個飯糰。舅舅悄悄地送了她一杯湯。「待人親切也是我工作的一部分。」他跟我說。我真的很以他為榮。

passages.title: 夜市的幸運魷魚
passages.text: Every Friday night, my family goes to the Shilin Night Market. Our favorite food stand belongs to Mr. Wang, a funny {1}. He sells grilled squid, and he always remembers his {2}. "Big squid for the big boy!" he shouts when he sees me. Last month, the price of squid went up, and many small stands could not {3} to stay open. Mr. Wang was worried, but he had an idea. He started selling "lucky squid." If your squid has a star sticker on it, the next one is free. Now his line is longer {4} ever. People do not mind waiting, and they {5} the game as much as the food.

blanks.why: shopkeeper「（小店的）老闆」：王先生是一位很有趣的攤販老闆。throat（喉嚨）、lemon（檸檬）、sock（襪子）都不能用來形容一個人。
remember his customers「記得他的顧客」，後面說他一看到「我」就打招呼。noodles（麵）、pumpkins（南瓜）、toes（腳趾）不會被老闆叫「大男孩」。
can't afford to + 原形動詞「負擔不起做某事」：成本變高，很多小攤付不起錢繼續營業。boil、spell、sneeze 後面都不能接 to stay open。
longer than ever「比以往都長」，比較級 longer 後面接 than。about、because、just 都不能放在 ever 前面表示比較。
enjoy the game「享受這個遊戲」。boil（煮沸）、spell（拼字）、sneeze（打噴嚏）接 the game 都不通。

passages.zh: 每個星期五晚上，我們全家都會去士林夜市。我們最喜歡的攤子是王先生的，他是個很有趣的老闆。他賣烤魷魚，而且總是記得他的客人。「大魷魚給大男孩！」他一看到我就這樣大喊。上個月魷魚漲價了，很多小攤子付不起成本繼續做下去。王先生很擔心，不過他想到一個辦法：他開始賣「幸運魷魚」。如果你的魷魚上貼著星星貼紙，下一支就免費。現在他攤前的隊伍比以前更長了。大家都不介意等待，而且他們享受這個遊戲，就跟享受美食一樣。

passages.title: 遊戲金幣與爸爸的卡
passages.text: Last summer, my little brother Kevin played a phone game every day. One evening, Dad got a message from the bank: his {1} card had paid 8,000 dollars for game coins! Dad's face turned red. "Kevin, did you use my card?" Kevin started to {2}. "I thought the coins were free," he said. Dad called the game company. The {3} service worker on the phone was very kind. She said, "Many young players make this mistake. We can return the money this time." Dad was relieved, because our family could not {4} to lose so much money. After that, Dad {5} his password. Now Kevin has to ask before he buys anything online.

blanks.why: credit card「信用卡」：銀行通知爸爸的信用卡付了八千元。noodle（麵）、throat（喉嚨）、pumpkin（南瓜）都不能和 card 組成付款工具。
start to + 原形動詞：Kevin 開始哭 cry。fry（油炸）、spell（拼字）、boil（煮沸）都不能表示被罵時的反應。
customer service「客服」是固定說法：電話上的客服人員很親切。knee、lemon、sock 都不能放在 service worker 前面。
can't afford to + 原形動詞：家裡負擔不起損失這麼多錢。bake（烤）、spell、sneeze 都不能接 to lose。
change the password「更改密碼」。fried、boiled、sneezed 接 password 都不通。

passages.zh: 去年夏天，我弟弟 Kevin 每天都在玩手機遊戲。有一天晚上，爸爸收到銀行的訊息：他的信用卡付了八千元買遊戲金幣！爸爸的臉都氣紅了。「Kevin，你是不是用了我的卡？」Kevin 開始哭了起來。「我以為那些金幣是免費的。」他說。爸爸打電話給遊戲公司，電話那頭的客服人員很親切。她說：「很多年紀小的玩家都會犯這種錯，這次我們可以退錢給您。」爸爸鬆了一口氣，因為我們家可承受不起損失這麼多錢。之後，爸爸改了密碼。現在 Kevin 在網路上買任何東西之前都得先問。

passages.title: 會說話的貓老闆
passages.text: In a small town, there was a magic shop with no sign. The {1} was an old cat who could talk. He sold strange things, like shoes that could run by themselves and a hat that made you invisible. One day, a poor girl named Nora came in. She wanted a magic map to find her lost dog. "It costs one gold coin," said the cat. Nora looked into her empty pocket. She could not {2} it. "Then pay me with a song," the cat said. Nora sang a song her grandma taught her. The cat {3} because the song reminded him of his old owner. He gave her the map for free. "You are my best {4} today," he said with a smile. With the map, Nora {5} her dog that same evening.

blanks.why: shopkeeper「店主」：這間魔法店的老闆是一隻會說話的老貓。spoon（湯匙）、fever（發燒）、belt（皮帶）都不能說是 an old cat。
can't afford + 物：口袋空空，買不起地圖。fry、spell、sneeze 接 it（地圖）都不通。
cried「哭了」：歌讓貓想起舊主人而哭。boiled（煮沸）、fried（油炸）、spelled（拼字）都不能表示聽歌後的情緒反應。
my best customer「我最好的顧客」：女孩來買東西，所以是顧客。noodle、knee、lemon 都不能指人。
found her dog「找到她的狗」，呼應前面要找走失的狗。baked、boiled、spelled 接 her dog 都不合理。

passages.zh: 在一個小鎮裡，有一間沒有招牌的魔法店。店主是一隻會說話的老貓。他賣一些奇怪的東西，像是會自己跑的鞋子，還有戴上就會隱形的帽子。有一天，一個名叫 Nora 的窮女孩走進店裡，她想要一張魔法地圖來找她走失的狗。「一枚金幣。」貓說。Nora 看了看自己空空的口袋，她買不起。「那就用一首歌來付吧。」貓說。Nora 唱了一首奶奶教她的歌。貓哭了，因為這首歌讓他想起以前的主人。他把地圖免費送給她。「你是我今天最好的客人。」他笑著說。靠著這張地圖，Nora 當天晚上就找到了她的狗。

passages.title: 職業體驗日的收銀台
passages.text: On Career Day, our class visited a big bookstore. Each student worked there for two hours. I was a {1} at the front desk. At first, I was very nervous. My first {2} was an old man who wanted a book about birds. I could not find it on the computer, so I asked my boss for help. Then a woman wanted to pay with her {3} card, but I did not know how to use the machine. She {4} patiently while I learned. By the end of the day, my feet hurt, but I felt proud. Now when I go shopping, I am always {5} to the people who work in stores. Their job is harder than it looks.

blanks.why: clerk「店員」：我在櫃台當店員。cough（咳嗽）、pumpkin（南瓜）、toe（腳趾）都不能當工作職位。
my first customer「我的第一位顧客」是一位老先生。spoon、fever、sock 都不能指人。
pay with a credit card「用信用卡付款」。throat（喉嚨）、noodle（麵）、knee（膝蓋）都不能和 card 搭配成付款方式。
waited patiently「耐心地等」：我在學怎麼用機器時她耐心地等。fried、boiled、sneezed 接 patiently 都不通。
be polite to + 人「對某人有禮貌」。salty（鹹的）、spicy（辣的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能用來形容對人的態度。

passages.zh: 職業體驗日那天，我們班去參觀一家大書店，每個學生都在那裡工作兩個小時。我在櫃台當店員，一開始非常緊張。我的第一位客人是一位想找鳥類書籍的老先生。我在電腦上找不到，只好請老闆幫忙。接著有一位女士想用信用卡付款，但我不會操作那台機器。她在我學的時候耐心地等著。那天結束時我的腳好痠，但我覺得很驕傲。現在我去買東西時，總是對店裡的工作人員很有禮貌。他們的工作比看起來還辛苦。

passages.title: 月球上的第一家商店
passages.text: In the year 2090, the first shop on the moon opened. The {1}, a robot named Bolt, sold water, snacks, and space suits. Everything was very {2} because it had to come from Earth by rocket. A bottle of water cost 50 dollars! Most astronauts could not {3} to buy snacks every day. So Bolt had an idea. He started to grow vegetables in the shop. Soon, fresh tomatoes and beans were for sale at a low price. Bolt's shop became the most popular place on the moon. Every {4} left with a smile, and Bolt {5} that a good idea can be worth more than gold.

blanks.why: shopkeeper「店主」：店主是一個叫 Bolt 的機器人。knee、lemon、cough 都不能說是機器人，也不會賣東西。
expensive「昂貴的」：東西要用火箭從地球運來，一瓶水要 50 元，所以很貴。lazy（懶惰的）、rude（無禮的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能形容商品的價錢。
can't afford to buy「買不起」：太空人負擔不起每天買零食。spell、boil、sneeze 都不能接 to buy。
every customer「每一位顧客」都笑著離開。spoon（湯匙）、toe（腳趾）、fever（發燒）不會「笑著離開」。
learned that…「學到…」：Bolt 學到好點子比黃金還值錢。fried、boiled、spelled 都不能接 that 子句。

passages.zh: 西元 2090 年，月球上第一家商店開張了。店主是一個名叫 Bolt 的機器人，他賣水、零食和太空衣。所有東西都很貴，因為都得用火箭從地球運過來，一瓶水就要 50 元！大部分的太空人都負擔不起每天買零食。於是 Bolt 想到一個辦法：他開始在店裡種菜。很快地，新鮮的番茄和豆子就以便宜的價格開賣了。Bolt 的店成了月球上最受歡迎的地方。每位客人都笑著離開，而 Bolt 也學到，一個好點子可能比黃金更值錢。

passages.title: 鞋店裡的灰姑娘
passages.text: In this story, Cinderella does not lose her shoe at a party. Instead, she works as a {1} at a shoe store in the city. One day, a young man comes in. He is a prince, but he is wearing old jeans, so nobody knows. He tries on ten pairs of shoes and says no to all of them. The other workers are {2} of him, but Cinderella stays patient. She finds him the perfect pair. When he pays with a golden {3} card, everyone is surprised. The next week, he comes back and {4} Cinderella to dinner. "You treat every {5} like a king," he says. "That is why I like you."

blanks.why: work as a clerk「當店員」：灰姑娘在鞋店當店員。throat（喉嚨）、bean（豆子）、sock（襪子）都不是工作職位。
be tired of + 人「對某人感到厭煩」：他試了十雙都不要，其他店員都受不了他。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能接 of him。
credit card「信用卡」：他用一張金色的信用卡付錢。noodle、knee、fever 都不能和 card 組成付款工具。
invite + 人 + to dinner「邀請某人吃晚餐」。fries、boils、spells 接人和 to dinner 都不通。
every customer「每一位顧客」：你把每個客人都當國王對待。spoon、pumpkin、toe 都不能被當成國王。

passages.zh: 在這個故事裡，灰姑娘沒有在舞會上掉了鞋子，而是在城裡一家鞋店當店員。有一天，一個年輕男子走進來。他是王子，但穿著舊牛仔褲，所以沒人認得出來。他試穿了十雙鞋，每一雙都說不要。其他店員都受不了他了，但灰姑娘始終很有耐心，幫他找到了最完美的一雙。當他拿出一張金色信用卡付錢時，大家都嚇了一跳。隔週，他又來了，還邀請灰姑娘去吃晚餐。「你把每一位客人都當成國王對待，」他說，「這就是我喜歡你的原因。」

passages.title: 存了三個月的籃球鞋
passages.text: Leo wanted a pair of new basketball shoes. They cost 4,000 dollars, and he could not {1} them. His mom said, "If you really want them, {2} your own money." So Leo stopped buying bubble tea and started walking dogs for his neighbors. Every week, he went to the sports shop to look at the shoes. The {3}, Mr. Chen, noticed him. "You are here again!" he laughed. Three months later, Leo finally had enough money. When he came to pay, Mr. Chen gave him a 20% discount. "You are my most patient {4}," he said. Leo wore the shoes in his next game and felt {5} every time he jumped.

blanks.why: can't afford + 物：鞋子要四千元，他買不起。spell、fry、sneeze 接 them（鞋子）都不通。
save money「存錢」：想要的話就自己存錢。fry（油炸）、spell（拼字）、boil（煮沸）接 money 都不合理。
shopkeeper「店老闆」：運動用品店的老闆陳先生注意到他。knee、lemon、cough 都不會「注意到」人、也不會笑著說話。
my most patient customer「我最有耐心的客人」。spoon、toe、fever 都不能指人。
feel proud「感到驕傲」：穿著自己存錢買的鞋，每次跳都很自豪。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容心情。

passages.zh: Leo 想要一雙新的籃球鞋。那雙鞋要四千元，他買不起。媽媽說：「如果你真的想要，就自己存錢吧。」於是 Leo 不再買珍珠奶茶，還開始幫鄰居遛狗。他每個星期都會去運動用品店看那雙鞋。店老闆陳先生注意到了他。「你又來啦！」他笑著說。三個月後，Leo 終於存夠了錢。他來付錢時，陳先生給了他八折優惠。「你是我最有耐心的客人。」他說。Leo 在下一場比賽穿上那雙鞋，每次跳起來都覺得很驕傲。

passages.title: 姊姊的飲料店奇遇
passages.text: My sister Amy works part-time as a {1} at a bubble tea shop. She says the hardest part of the job is the strange orders. One {2} asked for tea with no ice, no sugar, and no tea. "So… just a cup of pearls?" Amy asked. "Yes, please!" he said. Another girl ordered ten drinks and then said she forgot her wallet. She asked if she could pay by {3} card, but the shop only takes cash. In the end, her friend paid. Even so, Amy {4} her job. "Every day is like a comedy show," she says. "And I get one free drink after work. That is my {5} part!"

blanks.why: work as a clerk「當店員」：姊姊在飲料店打工當店員。pumpkin、throat、belt 都不是職位。
one customer「有一位顧客」點了很奇怪的飲料。noodle（麵）、knee（膝蓋）、sock（襪子）不會點飲料。
pay by credit card「用信用卡付款」，後面說店裡只收現金，前後對照。fever、lemon、toe 都不能和 card 組成付款方式。
enjoy her job「喜歡她的工作」。fries、boils、spells 接 her job 都不通。
my favorite part「我最喜歡的部分」：下班可以拿一杯免費飲料。salty、sour、thirsty 都不能形容「部分」表示喜好。

passages.zh: 我姊姊 Amy 在一家手搖飲店打工當店員。她說這份工作最難的是奇怪的點單。有一位客人點了去冰、無糖，而且不要茶的茶。「所以……只要一杯珍珠？」Amy 問。「對，麻煩你！」他說。還有一個女生點了十杯飲料，然後才說她忘了帶錢包。她問能不能刷卡，但店裡只收現金，最後是她朋友付的錢。即使如此，Amy 還是很喜歡她的工作。「每天都像在看喜劇表演，」她說，「而且下班還能拿一杯免費飲料，那是我最喜歡的部分！」

passages.title: 秋葉原的抽獎
passages.text: During our trip to Tokyo, my brother and I visited a huge anime shop in Akihabara. It had eight floors of toys, comics, and games. My brother wanted a Pikachu doll, but it cost 6,000 yen. "I can't {1} it," he said sadly. A friendly {2} heard us. She spoke a little English and told us about a lucky draw on the top floor. For 500 yen, you could win a prize. My brother tried and {3} a small Pikachu key ring. He was so {4} that he jumped up and down. The other {5} all clapped for him, and he smiled all the way back to the hotel.

blanks.why: can't afford it「買不起它」：娃娃要六千日圓，弟弟買不起。boil、spell、fry 接 it（娃娃）都不通。
a friendly clerk「一位親切的店員」聽到我們說話，還告訴我們抽獎的事。toe、bean、cough 都不會說英文。
got a key ring「得到一個鑰匙圈」。fried、boiled、spelled 接鑰匙圈都不合理。
so excited that…「興奮到…」：他興奮得跳上跳下。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容心情。
the other customers「其他客人」為他鼓掌。spoons、knees、lemons 都不會拍手。

gloss: 秋葉原（東京的電器與動漫街）
passages.zh: 我們去東京旅行時，我和弟弟逛了秋葉原一家超大的動漫商店，裡面有八層樓的玩具、漫畫和遊戲。弟弟想要一個皮卡丘娃娃，但要六千日圓。「我買不起。」他難過地說。一位親切的店員聽到了。她會說一點英文，告訴我們頂樓有抽獎活動，花五百日圓就有機會得到獎品。弟弟試了一次，抽到一個小小的皮卡丘鑰匙圈。他興奮得跳上跳下，其他客人都為他鼓掌，他一路笑著回到飯店。

passages.title: 巷口的二手書店
passages.text: There is a tiny used bookstore at the end of my street. The {1} is an eighty-year-old man named Mr. Hsu. His shop has no computer. He {2} where every book is, even though there are thousands of them. Many of his {3} are students. New books are expensive, and most of us cannot {4} to buy them all the time. At Mr. Hsu's shop, a book costs only fifty dollars. Sometimes he even gives books away for free. "Books are like friends," he always says. "They should not sit alone on a shelf." Last week, I found an old comic from 1985 there. Mr. Hsu smiled and said, "That one was mine when I was young. Take {5} of it."

blanks.why: shopkeeper「店老闆」：小書店的老闆是一位八十歲的老先生。spoon、lemon、cough 都不能說是一位老先生。
remember where…「記得…在哪裡」：沒有電腦，他卻記得每本書的位置。fries、boils、spells 都不能接 where 子句。
his customers「他的顧客」很多是學生。noodles、knees、socks 不能說是學生。
can't afford to buy「買不起」：新書很貴，我們不能常常買。sneeze、spell、boil 都不能接 to buy。
take care of「照顧、好好保管」是固定片語。soup、fever、toe 不能和 take…of 組成片語。

passages.zh: 我家這條街的盡頭有一間小小的二手書店。老闆是一位八十歲、姓許的老先生。他的店裡沒有電腦，但他記得每一本書放在哪裡，即使書有好幾千本。他的客人很多是學生。新書很貴，我們大部分的人沒辦法常常買。在許爺爺的店裡，一本書只要五十元，有時候他甚至會把書免費送人。「書就像朋友，」他總是這麼說，「不該孤零零地待在書架上。」上星期，我在那裡發現一本 1985 年的舊漫畫。許爺爺笑著說：「那本是我年輕時候的。好好照顧它。」

passages.title: 會打招呼的鸚鵡
passages.text: Our neighborhood pet shop has a special worker: a parrot named Kiki. Every time a {1} walks in, Kiki says, "Welcome! Welcome!" Children love her, and some families come to the shop just to {2} her talk. The real {3}, a young woman named Jenny, says Kiki is better at business than she is. One day, a boy asked how much Kiki cost. "She is not for sale," Jenny said. "Even a rich man could not {4} her. She is part of our family." The boy looked {5}, so Kiki said, "Come back tomorrow! Come back tomorrow!" Everyone laughed, and the boy promised he would.

blanks.why: a customer walks in「一位顧客走進來」，鸚鵡就說歡迎光臨。bean、throat、belt 都不會走進店裡。
hear her talk「聽牠說話」。fry、boil、spell 接 her talk 都不通。
the real clerk「真正的店員」是一位叫 Jenny 的年輕女生，和鸚鵡「特別的員工」對比。spoon、knee、lemon 不能指人。
can't afford + 物：就算有錢人也買不起牠，表示牠是無價的。sneeze、boil、spell 接 her 都不通。
look disappointed「看起來很失望」：鸚鵡不賣，男孩很失望。salty、sour、spicy 是味道，不能形容表情。

passages.zh: 我們社區的寵物店有一位特別的員工：一隻叫 Kiki 的鸚鵡。每當有客人走進來，Kiki 就會說：「歡迎！歡迎！」小朋友都很喜歡牠，有些家庭甚至專程來店裡聽牠說話。真正的店員是一位叫 Jenny 的年輕女生，她說 Kiki 比她還會做生意。有一天，一個男孩問 Kiki 要多少錢。「牠不賣喔，」Jenny 說，「就算是有錢人也買不起牠，牠是我們家的一份子。」男孩看起來很失望，於是 Kiki 說：「明天再來！明天再來！」大家都笑了，男孩也答應他會再來。

passages.title: 只用現金的阿公
passages.text: My grandpa does not trust {1} cards. "If you can't see the money, you will spend too much," he says. He always pays with cash, and he keeps it in an old leather wallet. Last month, we went to a department store together. Grandpa wanted to buy a new watch. The {2} said, "This one is on sale today, but only if you pay by card." Grandpa frowned. "Then I will pay the full price," he said. "I can {3} it, and I don't need a card." The clerk was surprised, but Grandpa looked proud. On the way home, he {4} me his rule: "Never buy something you can't pay for today." I think his rule is {5}.

blanks.why: credit card「信用卡」：阿公不相信信用卡，看不到錢就會花太多。pumpkin、fever、sock 不能組成付款用的卡片。
the clerk「店員」告訴他今天刷卡才有特價。toe、noodle、cough 不會說話介紹商品。
can afford it「付得起」：我買得起，不需要用卡。spell、boil、sneeze 接 it（手錶）都不通。
teach + 人 + 物「教某人某事」：他教我他的原則。fried、boiled、spelled 不能接「人＋物」。
wise「有智慧的」：我覺得他的原則很有道理。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容原則。

passages.zh: 我阿公不相信信用卡。「看不到錢，你就會花太多。」他說。他總是付現金，錢都放在一個舊皮夾裡。上個月，我們一起去百貨公司，阿公想買一支新手錶。店員說：「這支今天有特價，但只限刷卡。」阿公皺起眉頭。「那我就付全額，」他說，「我付得起，不需要卡。」店員很驚訝，但阿公看起來很驕傲。回家路上，他教了我他的原則：「今天付不出錢的東西，就永遠別買。」我覺得他的原則很有智慧。

passages.title: 沒有店員的超市
passages.text: A new supermarket opened near my house, and it has no cashiers at all. {1} scan their own food and pay at a machine. My mom loves it because she doesn't have to {2} in long lines. But my grandma hates it. The first time she went there, she pressed the wrong button ten times. "Where is the {3}? I need a real person!" she shouted. Finally, a young worker came over to help her. He showed her how to scan things and how to pay with her {4} card. Now Grandma goes there every week. She still does not like the machines, but she likes the young man. "He is very {5}," she says, "and he always helps me first."

blanks.why: Customers「顧客」自己掃描商品、在機器付錢。Spoons、Knees、Lemons 都不會自己結帳。
don't have to wait in line「不用排隊等」。fry、boil、spell 接 in long lines 都不通。
Where is the clerk?「店員在哪裡？」阿嬤需要真人幫忙。bean、throat、belt 都不是人。
pay with a credit card「刷信用卡付款」。noodle、fever、toe 都不能和 card 組成付款方式。
polite「有禮貌的」：他很有禮貌，總是先幫我。salty、sour、bitter 都是味道，不能用來形容人。

passages.zh: 我家附近開了一間新超市，裡面完全沒有收銀員。客人要自己掃描商品，再到機器付錢。我媽媽很喜歡，因為她不用排長長的隊。但我阿嬤很討厭這間超市。她第一次去的時候，按錯按鈕按了十次。「店員在哪裡？我需要一個真人！」她大叫。最後，一位年輕員工過來幫她，教她怎麼掃描商品、怎麼用信用卡付款。現在阿嬤每個星期都會去那裡。她還是不喜歡那些機器，但她喜歡那個年輕人。「他很有禮貌，」她說，「而且總是第一個來幫我。」

passages.title: 媽媽的早餐店
passages.text: My mom runs a small breakfast shop near the train station. She gets up at four every morning to make egg pancakes and sandwiches. As the {1}, she knows almost every {2} by name. "Mr. Lee, the usual? Black tea, no sugar?" she asks with a smile. Some of her customers are students who don't have much money. Mom knows they can't {3} a big meal, so she gives them extra eggs for free. Dad says she will lose money this way. But Mom just {4} and says, "A happy kid studies better." Last year, one of those students came back. He was a doctor now, and he {5} Mom a big cake to say thank you.

blanks.why: As the shopkeeper「身為老闆」，她認得幾乎每位客人。knee、spoon、cough 不能指人。
every customer「每一位客人」，後面她叫出李先生的名字。lemon、sock、fever 都沒有名字可以叫。
can't afford a big meal「吃不起一頓豐盛的餐」，所以媽媽多送蛋。spell、sneeze、boil 接 a big meal 都不通。
laughs「笑一笑」：媽媽只是笑著說…。fries、boils、spells 都不能接 and says 表示說話前的反應。
bring + 人 + 物「帶東西給某人」：他帶了一個大蛋糕給媽媽。fried、boiled、spelled 不能接「人＋物」。

passages.zh: 我媽媽在火車站附近經營一家小小的早餐店。她每天早上四點起床做蛋餅和三明治。身為老闆，她幾乎叫得出每一位客人的名字。「李先生，老樣子嗎？紅茶不加糖？」她笑著問。她有些客人是沒什麼錢的學生。媽媽知道他們吃不起豐盛的早餐，所以會免費多加蛋給他們。爸爸說這樣會虧錢，但媽媽只是笑笑說：「吃飽的孩子比較會讀書。」去年，其中一個學生回來了。他現在是醫生，還帶了一個大蛋糕來向媽媽道謝。

passages.title: 遊戲裡的道具商人
passages.text: In my favorite online game, there is a {1} named Old Tom. He sells swords, armor, and magic potions in the first village. Every new player visits his shop before going on an adventure. When I started playing, I only had ten gold coins. I wanted the dragon sword, but it cost five hundred. I could not {2} it. Old Tom said, "Go and {3} some slimes first. Come back when you are stronger." So I did. It took me two weeks, but I finally bought the sword. Old Tom said his usual line: "Thank you, brave {4}!" I know he is just a computer character, but I felt very {5} when he said it.

blanks.why: a shopkeeper「商店老闆」：他在村子裡賣劍和藥水。throat、bean、toe 都不能說是一個角色。
can't afford it「買不起」：只有十個金幣，劍要五百。boil、spell、sneeze 接 it 都不通。
fight some slimes「去打一些史萊姆」。fry、boil、spell 接 slimes 都不是遊戲中變強的方法。
brave customer「勇敢的客人」：玩家來店裡買東西，所以是客人。spoon、lemon、sock 都不能用「勇敢的」來稱呼。
feel proud「感到驕傲」。salty、sour、thirsty 都不能形容被稱讚時的心情。

passages.zh: 在我最喜歡的線上遊戲裡，有一位叫老湯姆的商店老闆。他在第一個村莊賣劍、盔甲和魔法藥水，每個新手玩家出發冒險前都會先去他的店。我剛開始玩的時候只有十個金幣。我想要那把龍之劍，但它要五百金幣，我買不起。老湯姆說：「先去打一些史萊姆吧，等你變強了再回來。」我照做了。花了兩個星期，我終於買到那把劍。老湯姆說出他的招牌台詞：「謝謝你，勇敢的客人！」我知道他只是電腦裡的角色，但聽到他這樣說，我還是覺得很驕傲。

passages.title: 墾丁的紀念品
passages.text: On our graduation trip to Kenting, everyone wanted to buy gifts for their families. I had only 500 dollars left. In a small shop, I saw a beautiful glass bottle with sand and tiny shells inside. It cost 800 dollars, so I could not {1} it. I put it back on the shelf. The {2}, a kind old lady, saw my face. "Is it for your mom?" she asked. I nodded. She showed me how to make my own bottle with sand from the {3} for only 100 dollars. I spent half an hour on it. Other {4} stopped to watch me. When I gave the bottle to Mom, she said it was the most {5} gift she had ever received.

blanks.why: can't afford it：只剩五百元，瓶子要八百，所以買不起。spell、boil、sneeze 接 it 都不通。
the clerk「店員」是一位親切的老太太。knee、noodle、cough 都不是人。
sand from the beach「海灘的沙」。fever（發燒）、throat（喉嚨）、toe（腳趾）都不會有沙子可以拿來做瓶子。
other customers「其他客人」停下來看我做。spoons、socks、lemons 不會停下來看。
the most special gift「最特別的禮物」。salty、sour、thirsty 都不能形容一份親手做的禮物。

passages.zh: 畢業旅行去墾丁時，大家都想買禮物給家人。我只剩五百元。在一家小店裡，我看到一個漂亮的玻璃瓶，裡面裝著沙子和小貝殼。它要八百元，我買不起，只好把它放回架上。店員是一位親切的老奶奶，她看到我的表情，問：「是要送媽媽的嗎？」我點點頭。她教我用海灘的沙自己做一瓶，只要一百元。我花了半個小時做，其他客人都停下來看。當我把瓶子送給媽媽時，她說那是她收過最特別的禮物。

passages.title: 冰淇淋車的音樂
passages.text: Every summer afternoon, an ice cream truck drives through our village. You can hear its music from far away. The {1}, Uncle Ming, has been selling ice cream for thirty years. When the music plays, children run out of their houses with coins in their hands. Uncle Ming's ice cream is cheap, so every kid can {2} it. One hot day, the truck broke down in front of my house. Uncle Ming was {3} because the ice cream would melt. So my dad called all our neighbors. In ten minutes, more than fifty {4} came, and everything was sold out. Uncle Ming laughed and said it was the best {5} of his life.

blanks.why: shopkeeper「老闆」：明叔賣冰淇淋三十年了。lemon、spoon、throat 都不能賣冰淇淋。
can afford it「買得起」：冰淇淋很便宜，每個小孩都買得起。spell、sneeze、boil 接 it 都不通。
be worried「擔心」：車子壞了，冰淇淋會融化。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容心情。
fifty customers「五十位客人」來買，東西就賣光了。knees、socks、fevers 都不會來買冰淇淋。
the best moment of his life「他人生中最棒的時刻」。soup、cough、toe 都不能用 the best… of his life 來形容一段經歷。

passages.zh: 每個夏天的午後，都有一台冰淇淋車開過我們村子，遠遠就能聽到它的音樂。老闆明叔已經賣冰淇淋三十年了。音樂一響，小孩子們就握著硬幣從家裡衝出來。明叔的冰淇淋很便宜，每個孩子都買得起。有一個大熱天，冰淇淋車在我家門口拋錨了。明叔很擔心，因為冰淇淋會融化。於是我爸爸打電話給所有鄰居。不到十分鐘，就來了五十多位客人，東西全部賣光。明叔笑著說，那是他這輩子最棒的時刻。

passages.title: 便利商店的小偵探
passages.text: Ella wants to be a detective one day. On Saturday, she was buying milk at a convenience store when a man in sunglasses came in. He bought a phone and paid with a {1} card. The {2} asked him to sign his name. Ella noticed something {3}. The name on the card was "Mary Brown," but he signed "Mike." Ella quietly told the store manager. The manager called the police. Later, they learned the card was stolen! The police thanked Ella. "You are a very careful {4}," one officer said. Ella was so happy that she could not {5} smiling for the rest of the day.

blanks.why: paid with a credit card「用信用卡付款」，後面提到卡上的名字。bean、knee、sock 都不能和 card 組成付款工具。
the clerk「店員」請他簽名。noodle、cough、toe 都不會請人簽名。
something strange「奇怪的事」：卡上的名字和簽名不一樣。salty、sour、spicy 都是味道，不能形容她注意到的事情。
a careful customer「細心的顧客」：Ella 是來買牛奶的客人。spoon、lemon、throat 都不能用來稱讚人。
can't stop + V-ing「忍不住一直…」：她開心得一直笑。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 smiling。

passages.zh: Ella 夢想有一天能當偵探。星期六，她在便利商店買牛奶時，一個戴墨鏡的男人走了進來。他買了一支手機，用信用卡付錢。店員請他簽名。Ella 注意到一件奇怪的事：卡片上的名字是「Mary Brown」，他卻簽了「Mike」。Ella 悄悄告訴店長，店長就報了警。後來大家才知道那張卡是偷來的！警察向 Ella 道謝。「你是一位非常細心的顧客。」一位警官說。Ella 開心得那天一整天都笑個不停。

passages.title: 可以賒帳的雜貨店
passages.text: Fifty years ago, my grandpa's village had only one small store. The {1}, Mrs. Lin, sold rice, oil, soap, and candy. Most families were poor, and many could not {2} to pay right away. So Mrs. Lin let them buy on {3}. She wrote every family's name and what they owed in a thick notebook. When the harvest came, people paid her back. "Nobody ever ran away," Grandpa said. "We all {4} each other." Today, Mrs. Lin's old notebook is in the village museum. Grandpa took me to see it last year. His father's name is on page twelve. Seeing it made me {5} close to the family I never met.

blanks.why: shopkeeper「店主」：林太太在村裡開雜貨店。pumpkin、fever、belt 都不能賣東西。
can't afford to pay「付不出錢」：很多家庭窮，沒辦法馬上付錢。spell、sneeze、boil 都不能接 to pay。
buy on credit「賒帳」是固定說法：先拿東西，之後再付錢。soup、knee、lemon 不能放在 buy on 後面。
trust each other「互相信任」：從來沒有人跑掉。fried、boiled、spelled 接 each other 都不通。
make + 人 + feel…「讓某人覺得…」。fry、boil、spell 都不能接 close 表示感受。

passages.zh: 五十年前，我阿公住的村子只有一家小雜貨店。店主林太太賣米、油、肥皂和糖果。大部分的家庭都很窮，很多人沒辦法馬上付錢，所以林太太讓大家賒帳。她把每一戶的名字和欠的錢都寫在一本厚厚的筆記本裡。等到收成的時候，大家再把錢還給她。「從來沒有人跑掉過，」阿公說，「我們都互相信任。」現在，林太太的舊筆記本放在村裡的博物館。阿公去年帶我去看，他父親的名字就在第十二頁。看到它，讓我覺得和那些從沒見過的家人好親近。
